# Slydekit

> Simple yet powerful presentation framework for Typst.

## Pages

- [Alternatives](https://maucejo.github.io/slydekit/animations/alternatives.html): The alternatives function allows you to display different content per step.
- [Animation system](https://maucejo.github.io/slydekit/animations/anim.html): The animation system in Slydekit allows you to create dynamic and interactive presentations by controlling the visibility and behavior of content on slides.
- [Code animation](https://maucejo.github.io/slydekit/animations/code-reveal.html): The code animation feature allows you to highlight specific lines of code in a step-by-step manner during a presentation. This can be particularly useful for explaining complex code snippets or algorithms, as it enables the presenter to focus the audience's attention on one part…
- [CeTZ/Fletcher integration](https://maucejo.github.io/slydekit/animations/draw-reveal.html): As mentioned in , uncover and only are not compatible with packages like CeTZ or Fletcher. The reason is that CeTZ and Fletcher have their own rendering mechanisms and context. Therefore, Slydekit cannot simply wrap the content with hide() as it does for regular Typst content.
- [One by one/Item by item](https://maucejo.github.io/slydekit/animations/item.html): Using pausecan be tedious when you have a list of words or items that you want to reveal one by one. Slydekit provides two convenient functions, one-by-one and item-by-item, to simplify this process.
- [Meanwhile and track](https://maucejo.github.io/slydekit/animations/meanwhile.html): Sometimes, you want to show multiple things at the same time, but not necessarily all of them. For example, you might want to show a list of items, and then reveal them one by one, but also have some items that are always visible. This is where the #meanwhile and #track commands…
- [Pause, uncover and only](https://maucejo.github.io/slydekit/animations/pause.html): This page describes the pause, uncover and only animations available in Slydekit. These animations are used to control the visibility of content on slides, allowing for dynamic presentations.
- [Appendix](https://maucejo.github.io/slydekit/components/appendix.html): If you want to add additional content to your presentation, you can use the appendix function. This function allows you to create an appendix section in your presentation, which can be used to include supplementary information, references, or any other content that is not part of…
- [Bibliography](https://maucejo.github.io/slydekit/components/bibliography.html): Slydekit provides a built-in bibliography feature that allows you to manage and display references in your presentation. You can use the built-in Typst #bibliography function to include a bibliography section in your slides, and the #footcite function to create footnotes for…
- [Callout boxes](https://maucejo.github.io/slydekit/components/callout-boxes.html): Callout boxes are a way to highlight important information in your presentation. They can be used to draw attention to key points, provide additional context, or emphasize warnings and tips.
- [Handout mode](https://maucejo.github.io/slydekit/components/handout.html): The handout mode in Slydekit allows you to create a version of your presentation that is suitable for printing or sharing as a PDF. This mode is designed to provide a more compact and readable format, making it easier for your audience to follow along with your presentation.
- [Localization](https://maucejo.github.io/slydekit/components/localization.html): The localization feature in Slydekit allows you to create presentations in different languages. You can specify the language of your presentation using the lang parameter in the slydekit function. The default language is English ("en"), but you can change it to any supported…
- [Miscellaneous](https://maucejo.github.io/slydekit/components/miscellaneous.html): Slydekit provides a set of additional functions that can be useful in various scenarios, particularly when creating your own theme.
- [Slides](https://maucejo.github.io/slydekit/components/slides.html): The main building block of the Slydekit framework is the slide function, which is used to create individual slides in a presentation.
- [Getting started](https://maucejo.github.io/slydekit/getting-started.html): This section introduces the basic workflow for creating presentations with Slydekit. You will first learn how to import the template and configure the main presentation settings. Then, a minimal example will demonstrate the core structure of a Slydekit document, including how to…
- [Slydekit Documentation](https://maucejo.github.io/slydekit/): Slydekit is a Typst presentation template designed to make slide creation simple and flexible. Its theme system, inspired by Bookly, makes it straightforward to design and integrate new themes.
- [Outlines](https://maucejo.github.io/slydekit/navigation/outline.html): In Slydekit, you can create an outline using the tableofcontents command.
- [Progress bars](https://maucejo.github.io/slydekit/navigation/progress-bars.html): Slydekit provides progress bars to indicate either the progress of the section or the progress of the entire presentation. These function are intended to be used in a custom theme.
- [Topbar/Minislide](https://maucejo.github.io/slydekit/navigation/topbar.html): Slydekit provides optional navigation elements to help structure and navigate presentations. The topbar displays the presentation’s content as a persistent navigation bar, highlighting the current section to provide a clear overview of the presentation structure. The minislide…
- [Built-in themes](https://maucejo.github.io/slydekit/theming/built-in-themes.html): Slydekit provides a set of built-in themes that you can use to customize the appearance of your presentations. Each theme defines a unique combination of colors, fonts, and layout styles, allowing you to create visually appealing slides with minimal effort.
- [Custom themes](https://maucejo.github.io/slydekit/theming/custom-themes.html): Using one of the built-in themes, presented in Built-in Themes is a great way to get started with Slydekit, but you may want to create your own custom theme to match your branding or personal style. This section will guide you through the process of creating a custom theme and…
- [Fonts and colors](https://maucejo.github.io/slydekit/theming/fonts-colors.html): Sometimes, you may want to use a built-in theme, but customize the fonts and colors used in your presentation to match your branding or personal preferences. Slydekit allows you to easily override the default fonts and colors by providing your own definitions.
